reason: The rule flags `/// <reference types="x" />` only when x is also the specifier of a static import in the same file. Shared metavariable bindings (M2) do not reach it: x lives inside a comment token, and a metavariable binds whole nodes, never a regex capture, so the directive's name cannot be joined with an import's string. New token regex-capture-metavar: a regex capture group that binds a metavariable. The port flags every reference-types directive in a file that has any import (select_when gate); the directive regex is line-anchored and the finding sits on the name through a named group (capture.NAME).

evidence.why: `/// <reference types="bar" />`: no import of "bar", but the file imports other modules, so the gate passes and the port reports a false positive
